full_citation: SC&A, Inc.; Rogers & Associates Engineering Corp.; Roy F. Weston, Inc. (1991, May). Diffuse NORM Wastes: Waste Characterization and Risk Assessment. DRAFT. Prepared for U.S. EPA Office of Radiation Programs (Contract 68-D90170, Work Assignment 1-59; managers W.E. Russo and J.M. Gruhlke). 478 pp. Precursor of EPA 402-R-93-083 (1993).
notes: READ (scanned PDF supplied by Steve; OCR text checked against page images for every number used). Chapter pages: B.1 uranium overburden B-1-1..B-1-23 (PDF pp.40-62); B.4 coal ash B-4-1..B-4-24 (PDF pp.114-137); B.5 oil and gas scale and sludge B-5-1..B-5-31 (PDF pp.142-172; PDF page = marker number in the OCR text = report page + 141 for B.5); B.8 geothermal B-8-1..B-8-20 (PDF pp.255-274); Table D.2-2 (PDF p.303) holds the reference pile parameters. Key O&G numbers: 20-year scale+sludge 4.6 million m3 = 8.3 million t (1.8 t/m3), from 620,000 US oil wells x 30 % contaminated x 250 m3 per 10-well facility per 20 years (pp.B-5-16, B-5-20); ES-5 says 'about 360,000 m3 yearly' (inconsistent with 4.6e6/20 = 230,000 m3/a); weighted Ra-226 155 and Ra-228 55 pCi/g (5.7 and 2.0 Bq/g), Pb-210 = Po-210 = Ra-226 and Th-228 = Ra-228 assumed in equilibrium (p.B-5-23/24); gamma-survey distribution of Ra-226 median 6, mean 125, 90th 250, 99th 2,615, maximum 37,500 pCi/g (p.B-5-23/24); Rn-222 emanation 0.1 (p.B-5-24). NO scale/sludge mass split and NO disposal-route percentages are given. Coal: 1987 ash 62.55 Mt, 26.5 % used (Table B.4-4), weighted ash Ra-226 3.7 pCi/g (p.B-4-19). Uranium: overburden Ra-226 23.7 pCi/g, flux mean 11.1 pCi/m2/s (pp.B-1-19/20). This is a DRAFT: the numbers differ from the final 1993 report (see S1209 correction). OCR faults recorded in research/oil_gas/papers_round3.md section 1.

full_citation: Johnson, R.H., Jr., Bernhardt, D.E., Nelson, N.S., Galley, H.W., Jr. (1973, November). Assessment of potential radiological health effects from radon in natural gas. EPA-520/1-73-004. U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Office of Radiation Programs, Washington, D.C. 72 pp.
notes: READ in full (PDF supplied by Steve; printed page = PDF page - 10; Tables 1, 2 and 4 checked against page images). Table 1 (p.5) wellhead Rn-222 averages: Gulf Coast (LA, TX) 5, Kansas 100, Wyoming 10, SW Colorado/NW New Mexico 25, Texas/Kansas/Oklahoma <100 (range 5-1,450), Texas Panhandle range 10-520 pCi/L; unweighted overall average 37 pCi/L (1,369 Bq/m3). Table 4 (p.14) distribution-line averages: Chicago 14.4, New York 1.5, Denver 50.5, West Coast 15, Colorado 25, Nevada 8, New Mexico 45, Houston 8; overall 23 pCi/L (851 Bq/m3); report adopts 20 pCi/L (740 Bq/m3) for the US at point of use (10-100 range), 50 pCi/L near the Kansas-Colorado-New Mexico-Panhandle fields (pp.13, 36). Table 2 (p.6): 1971 US marketed production 19,532,622 and consumption 20,268,303 million ft3 with state/division percentages. LPG stripping removes 30-75 % of the radon (p.9, citing Fries and Kilgren 1972); Houston retail LPG annual means 25-180 pCi/L; New Mexico plant inlet 56 -> propane 1,100 pCi/L (p.9). Pipeline transit 10-12 miles/h, 1,500 miles = 1-2 half-lives (p.10). Contains NO retention fraction of 34 % (the only 0.34 is a ventilation multiplier on p.44). Dose and risk content ignored for Radiopassive (activity only).

The article gives ONLY 'about 25,000 tons of NORM-contaminated scale' and '225,000 tons of NORM-contaminated sludge' per year (reference 3: 'Draft of Diffuse NORM-Waste Characterization and Preliminary Risk Assessment', US EPA Office of Radiation and Indoor Air, 1993). Use S1250 as the primary, S1209 as a secondary on the 1993 draft; do not describe S1209 as the 1993 final report.
